To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) symbiosis is a major evolutionary force, (ii) the evolution of symbiosis is a complex and dynamic process, (iii) symbiotic systems are characterized by high rates of horizontal gene transfer, (iv) the evolution of complex symbiotic systems is driven by the evolution of host-symbiont coevolutionary interactions, and (v) symbiotic systems have the potential to evolve into new species.
The study of symbioses integrates the three domains of biology.
the study of symbiosis has led to the realization that the three domains of biology — archaea, bacteria, and eukaryotes — are not separate and independent, but rather are intimately intertwined.

understanding the nature and extent of symbiosis in the biotic world and how this affects the evolution, ecology and physiology of organisms and the biosphere.

how the interactions between organisms shape the evolution, development, and physiology of both symbiotic partners.
